findings.claim: No PMR/MDB parser or record schema identified in searched source, tests, research scripts or documents.
findings.qualification: This is a pinned-commit inspection, not a statement about other branches or future releases.

findings.claim: .pmr and .mdb have no classifier cases and fall through to unknown.
Project dispatch has configuration, AVB, AAF, ALE, EDL and media analysis, without PMR dispatch.
Technical media analysis invokes ffprobe, not a PMR decoder.
Python inspector offers probe, analyze-bin and analyze-aaf commands, using pyavb/pyaaf2.
Generic binary configuration inspection reports magic/hash/entropy/strings, not semantic PMR records.
Repository code license is MIT; copied substantial portions require preservation of copyright/permission notice.

github.execution: Downloaded source text only; no repository code or installation scripts were executed.

mdvx.method: Hopper pseudo-C plus arm64 instructions and Objective-C metadata; no timed MDVx scan.
confirmedPmrBehavior: NSOperation queue maximum 6; one operation per PMR. Bella requested 4 instead.
Whole PMR buffered once; serial cursor walk within a job.
Flat items retain selected fields plus mutable copies of PMR record slices.
Parser recognizes versions 2, 8 and 16 in inspected paths.
Parses both record sets then later deduplicates; exact duplicate winner not established.
Ordinary enrichment can open sibling msmMMOB.mdb, fallback amaMMOB.mdb, when ScanMDB is enabled.
Optional ScanMXF fallback is separate from PMR parsing.
Directory names listed once; subtract referenced/reserved names; per-file filesystem checks remain.
Missing or zero-count PMR prevents inspected directory-listing path.
Batch append uses short shared lock; parsing occurs outside it.
MDB lookup uses 8-byte identity excerpt at offset 16.

extensionGate.behavior: Require extension version16 and count equal to the original first-set count; otherwise warn/stop. Resets cursor count on success without adopting independent second count.
extensionGate.comparison: Native MC writer can legitimately emit unequal counts; none of six live PMRs exercises this difference.

textBranches.behavior: v16 filename and project use UTF-8 only when the first 16-bit payload word is zero; skip that prefix. Otherwise ASCII path. Ordinary legacy strings request ASCII.

limitations: No comparative timing or peak-memory benchmark; concurrency limit does not establish speedup.
No production source changed or Bella parser implemented.
Live samples are little-endian; no genuine v1, unequal-count, malformed or non-ASCII-filename PMR in this set.
Native static behavior for missing/invalid records must be distinguished from Bella inventory policy.
No universal legacy text codepage or historical DTM epoch established.
Temporary generated probes and decompilation stay outside repository documentation.

approvedBellaTextRule.userInstruction: OK understood. let's lock that in for Bella: use v16 set when usable, read Filename as UTF-8 and Project as MacRoman, and fall back to the older set only if v16 is missing or unusable.
approvedBellaTextRule.setSelection: Use a usable version-16 record set; use the older base set only if version 16 is missing or unusable. Select a whole set, not a Project-only fallback.

olderSet.project: MacRoman when stored; version 1 has no stored Project

approvedBellaTextRule.deferred: How Windows producers write Project names remains deferred. The usable-set and damage checks are now user-approved; see approvedBellaSetFallback. PMR DTM interpretation and use remain excluded.

approvedBellaModificationRule.rule: Ignore PMR DTM throughout Bella scanner/parser pipeline; bounded skip of four bytes only, no retention, date interpretation, time comparison or scan trigger.

mdvxIdentityFollowup.conclusion: MDVx stores full modern IDs but compares an eight-byte excerpt for MDB and ordinary bin matching. Ordinary duplicate-row equality also requires the same path.

approvedBellaIdentityRules.fullIds: Read complete FileMobId and MasterMobId, not only an eight-byte excerpt of modern IDs. Respect complete legacy representations when falling back.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.kelpieId: Retain current internal MediaMuster scan-session row identifier, independent of Avid IDs.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.samePathAndSameFileMobId: Ignore duplicate inventory entry; keep existing row and KelpieId.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.differentPathAndSameFileMobId: Keep each row with its own unique KelpieId.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.scope: Inventory row duplication; eligible metadata may still enrich the kept row. No new cross-scan persistence specified.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.samePathConflictingFileMobIds: For release one, the user explicitly assumes this cannot happen. Do not add conflict-handling machinery.

concurrencyClarification.unit: One PMR file per job, including its older and v16 sets. Up to four PMR jobs in progress at once.
concurrencyClarification.cpuMeaning: No reserved CPU/core count; workers are scheduled by the OS and may wait for storage. No speed multiplier established.
concurrencyClarification.notYetSelected: Worker implementation mechanism and later MDB/media-header concurrency.

binFilterScopeClarification.status: User scope clarification; existing Bin Filter system remains unchanged
binFilterScopeClarification.userInstruction: This scope is for the Scanner/parser system. We are leaving the Bin Filter system alone, just confirmed that MDVX also uses FileMobId to filter Bins.
binFilterScopeClarification.scope: Bella replaces the scanner/parser system only. The Bin Filter system is outside Bella and remains unchanged; no new bin algorithm, matching or per-row behavior is required.
binFilterScopeClarification.comparisonConfirmed: The inspected MDVx bin filtering uses FileMobId identity; that comparison does not approve changes to MediaMuster Bin Filter behavior.

approvedBellaSetFallback.userInstruction: For now, the first release of the app: lets keep it basic and straight forward. If an entry is damaged, abandon the set and fall back to another set. How should we determine this?
approvedBellaSetFallback.damagedRecord: Any damaged record makes its entire set unusable; do not salvage individual records or combine metadata from the two sets.
approvedBellaSetFallback.setSelection: Prefer a usable version-16 set. If it is missing or unusable, use the older set only if that whole set is usable.
approvedBellaSetFallback.neitherUsable: Use no PMR metadata when neither set is usable. Keep the physical media-file inventory independently.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationStatus: User-approved release-one damage and usability checks on 18 October 2026; not implemented.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationApproval: OK, let's lock those checks in for Bella.

approvedChecks.completeEntry: Every declared record must contain all bytes required by its supported version: complete IDs, length words and counted text payloads, and the four bounded skipped modification bytes. A short record makes its whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.lengthsAndCounts: Stored text lengths and record counts must fit the available data; an overrun or impossible count makes the whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.version16Filename: Require the verified v16 filename framing and strict UTF-8. Its two reserved prefix bytes must be present and the first zero; the native PMR helper does not constrain the second. Invalid framing or UTF-8 makes the whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.emptyFilename: An empty or null Filename makes the whole set unusable because it cannot associate that entry with a physical file. This is a Bella usability rule, not proof of structural corruption.
approvedChecks.emptySet: A set with no entries supplies no usable PMR metadata; fall back to the other usable set.

notDamage: Fields legitimately absent in older versions, including v1 Project and MasterMobId
Different entry counts between the older and version-16 sets
A database reference to a physical file that has since disappeared
approvedBellaSetFallback.safeVersion16Location: The older set physically precedes v16. Follow its lengths and counts safely to locate v16; if damaged framing makes that boundary unknowable, ignore PMR metadata rather than search for a plausible version word. Keep physical inventory.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationLimit: These checks cannot detect every incorrect value with a valid representation. MacRoman accepts every byte, so successful decoding does not prove a Project character is correct. Ignored modification values are not inspected for semantic validity.
